rows.requirement: An explicit body-bounded opt-in live Anthropic canary proves the reviewed real transport without repository or credential disclosure.
rows.rationale: The reviewed test-only one-attempt canary fixes endpoint, API version, model, harmless body, preflight, scoped-secret, response and resource bounds, and deterministic transport tests pass. The published production-disabled Windows checkpoint supplies an exact-reference, policy-before-read Credential Manager broker and Anthropic credential composition without enumeration. One owned reference was provisioned through a separate reviewed helper. The first approved canary returned an ambiguous unphased TRANSPORT_FAILURE and was not retried. Deterministic diagnosis found that provider and response errors thrown inside the secret callback were collapsed by the broker's finite consumer-error mapping; the repaired canary carries exact bounded callback outcomes through material disposal and reports conservative pre-dispatch, possibly-dispatched, response-received, or post-response phases. After publication, exact-head CI, frozen-boundary review, and exact availability preflight, one newly authorized attempt used a distinct durable marker, observed a provider response, and failed closed with TRANSPORT_FAILURE at response-received. It was not retried and is not the exact successful live transport proof, so the row remains incomplete.

rows.rationale: The separately committed Account Manager reader and exact-pinned AI OS adapter provide a maintained read-only protocol, explicit inactive-window evidence, bounded synthetic cross-repository proof, exact configuration/profile binding and no UI or credential authority. One authorized pre-repair read failed closed without store mutation before the protocol-v2/schema-v3 repair. That repair was then published on fix/stage-18-inactive-usage-window-contract and its first-party hosted packed-consumer gate passed on the exact source head (run 31897858353, job 95043852228) and again at the evidence head (run 31917172046, job 95090890714, attempt 1, all six jobs green). Under that green head the operator granted one separately authorized installed-state read, executed exactly once on 2026-08-16 through the maintained reader (commit f958ccae, tree 04c22c65, reader SHA-256 ba17ed90...b894, protocol v2, runtime 1.4.1) against the real store with one allowlisted owned profile, a 15-second deadline, no retry, no UI automation, no credential access and no directory enumeration. It returned a normalized schema-v3 authorized-profile snapshot: the required five-hour window was genuinely inactive and was projected as null-capacity non-allocatable evidence instead of refusing, the weekly window projected 8,800/1,200 basis points, and the snapshot honestly self-described as past freshUntil so downstream allocation still refuses fail-closed. Only the two named store files were opened and both were byte-identical before and after. That is the supported read-only live integration supplying authorized profile snapshots without UI or credential extraction, so the row is proven; a further read would require a new operator approval cycle.
